newsitem.title: UK: Pace says no confirmation on digital order.
newsitem.headline: Pace says no confirmation on digital order.

text.p: Pace Micro Technology confirmed on Thursday that it was one of the candidates to manufacture digital decoders for BSkyB but said that the satellite broadcaster had not advised it of firm plans for the service.
"Fifteen companies were invited to tender for the box and during negotiations these were whittled down to four. It seems like all four are going to get a slice of the cake," a Pace spokesman said.
He was commenting on a report in the Financial Times that BSkyB had decided to press ahead with the launch of 200-channel digital satellite services this autumn.
The report said that documents were being drawn up to order one million decoders at a cost of about 250 million pounds.
Negotiations were reported completed in all but detail with manufacturers Pace, Panasonic, Sony and Nokia.
The Pace spokesman said that BSkyB had not formally notified Pace of its digital plans. He noted that the report said that a BSkyB board meeting next Tuesday would approve the launch.
There was no comment from BSkyB.
